blueprint_concepts: Four points(Centroid, Incenter, circumcenter, orthocenter) of a triangle

concept_use.Four points(Centroid, Incenter, circumce: The circumcentre S and orthocentre H are the triangle centres used; angle BHC = 180 - A and angle BSC = 2A come from their properties.
concept_use.Circumradius and circumcenter based ques: Circumradius by the sine rule R = BC/(2 sin(angle)) for triangles HBC and SBC gives R2 = R and R1 = R/(2 cos A).

english: Let $A(1,2)$, $B(-2,6)$ and $C(7,10)$ be the vertices of triangle $ABC$, and let $S$ and $H$ be its circumcentre and orthocentre respectively. Let $R_1$ and $R_2$ be the circumradii of triangles $SBC$ and $HBC$ respectively. Then the value of $\dfrac{R_2}{R_1}$ is ______.
hindi: माना $A(1,2)$, $B(-2,6)$ तथा $C(7,10)$ त्रिभुज $ABC$ के शीर्ष हैं, तथा $S$ और $H$ क्रमशः इसके परिकेन्द्र और लम्बकेन्द्र हैं। माना $R_1$ तथा $R_2$ क्रमशः त्रिभुजों $SBC$ तथा $HBC$ की परित्रिज्याएँ हैं। तब $\dfrac{R_2}{R_1}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $\overrightarrow{AB}=(-3,4)$, $\overrightarrow{AC}=(6,8)$: $\cos A=\dfrac{-18+32}{5\cdot10}=\dfrac{7}{25}$; the triangle is acute (checks at $B$, $C$ positive)
$SB=SC=R$ and $\angle BSC=2A$, so $R_1=\dfrac{BC}{2\sin2A}=\dfrac{2R\sin A}{4\sin A\cos A}=\dfrac{R}{2\cos A}$
solution_full: At $B$: $\overrightarrow{BA}\cdot\overrightarrow{BC}=(3,-4)\cdot(9,4)=11>0$; at $C$: $\overrightarrow{CA}\cdot\overrightarrow{CB}=(-6,-8)\cdot(-9,-4)=86>0$. So the triangle is acute, $S$ and $H$ lie inside it.
Triangle $HBC$: in an acute triangle $\angle BHC=180^\circ-A$. By the sine rule its circumradius is $R_2=\dfrac{BC}{2\sin(180^\circ-A)}=\dfrac{BC}{2\sin A}=R$, the circumradius of $ABC$.
Triangle $SBC$: $SB=SC=R$ and the central angle is $\angle BSC=2A$. So $R_1=\dfrac{BC}{2\sin2A}$. With $BC=2R\sin A$: $R_1=\dfrac{2R\sin A}{4\sin A\cos A}=\dfrac{R}{2\cos A}$.
originality_note: New: the ratio of the circumradii of SBC and HBC is the invariant 2 cos A (way 4: hidden invariant), which makes a heavy coordinate computation collapse once the angle relations angle BHC = 180 - A and angle BSC = 2A are used. Closest known: 'the circumradius of HBC equals R'. Different because: it is combined with the central-angle triangle SBC, and the data are coordinates, so the student must see the angle route.
stem_review: Read as a student: every point, line, curve and symbol is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath (and a numerical brute-force check), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Checked the triangle is acute (so angle BSC = 2A, not 360 - 2A) and scalene. Changed: No change.
key_step: Recognising R(HBC) = R and R(SBC) = R/(2 cos A), so only cos A is needed.
justification: Two triangle-centre facts linked through the sine rule; the brute-force route is long, the idea route is short. Comparable to 2023-P2-Q15 (L4) in topic but much lighter; placed at L3 with 2021-P1-Q1 (L3).
